title: Clinical-context guidance and hyperbolic prototype learning for long-tailed radiology report generation.
abstract: Automated radiology report generation (RRG) can reduce the reporting burden, but existing methods remain limited in their ability to integrate clinical context effectively at the feature level. They also struggle with long-tailed disease distributions, which can hinder recognition of infrequent findings. To address these issues, CSMH-RRG, a clinically guided framework that integrates clinical semantic modulation (CSM) and hyperbolic prototype-based classification (HPC), is proposed. The CSM module conditions postencoder visual representations on patient-specific clinical context through semantic injection and channel recalibration. The HPC module represents multiple disease states as learnable prototypes on the Poincaré ball and converts predicted states into disease-state tokens for report generation. Under the primary MIMIC-CXR protocol, CSMH-RRG achieved a BLEU-4 score of 0.262 and a diseasewise macro CheXbert F1 score of 0.564, achieving state-of-the-art performance on clinical factuality metrics while maintaining comparable BLEU-4 performance to the best-performing baseline. When transferred from MIMIC-CXR to IU X-ray without fine tuning, it achieved a BLEU-4 score of 0.118 and a CE F1 score of 0.289. Specifically, in the MIMIC-CXR frequency-stratified classifier analysis, CSMH-RRG increased tail-group macro F1 from 35.5% to 41.4% relative to the linear baseline. Head-group macro F1 also increased from 72.1% to 73.5%. These results indicate that CSMH-RRG supports report generation and improves frequency-sensitive disease-state prediction within the evaluated benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/tinkerbellqwq/CSMH-RRG.

title: 177 Lu-Prostate-specific Membrane Antigen Prior to Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy in Oligorecurrent Prostate Cancer: Secondary and Exploratory End Point Results from the Randomized Phase 2 LUNAR Trial.
abstract: The phase 2 randomized LUNAR trial previously demonstrated that neoadjuvant 177 Lu-PNT2002 before stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with oligorecurrent hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (orHSPC). We report updated efficacy and safety outcomes with extended follow-up. Patients with prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT)-detected orHSPC and one to five metastatic lesions amenable to SBRT were randomized 1:1 to SBRT alone or two cycles of neoadjuvant 177 Lu-PNT2002 followed by SBRT. The primary end point was PFS, defined as new lesions on PSMA PET/CT, initiation of salvage hormonal therapy, or death. Secondary end points included hormonal therapy-free survival (HT-FS) and 24-mo progression-free status. Exploratory end points included polymetastatic PFS (poly-PFS), castration-resistant disease-free survival (CRFS), and conventional imaging progression-free survival (CT-PFS). Between September 2022 and November 2023, 92 patients were randomized to SBRT alone (n = 47) or 177 Lu-PNT2002 plus SBRT (n = 45). At a median follow-up of 31.9 mo, 177 Lu-PNT2002 significantly improved PFS (median 17.6 vs 7.4 mo; hazard ratio [HR] 0.38, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.23-0.61; p < 0.001) and HT-FS (HR 0.57, 95% CI = 0.34-0.95; p = 0.03). Exploratory analyses demonstrated improved poly-PFS (HR 0.28, 95% CI = 0.08-1.03; p = 0.04), CRFS (HR 0.13, 95% CI = 0.02-1.10; p = 0.03), and CT-PFS (HR 0.46, 95% CI = 0.19-1.09; p = 0.07). No new safety signals were observed. With extended follow-up, neoadjuvant 177 Lu-PNT2002 before SBRT produced durable improvements in PFS and HT-FS. While poly-PFS, CRFS, and CT-PFS were exploratory end points, their improvement provides hypothesis-generating evidence that the addition of radioligand therapy to SBRT may alter disease trajectory beyond delaying PSMA PET/CT-detected recurrence.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Triage in Primary Care: A Scoping Review of Clinical Applicability.
abstract: Aim To map artificial intelligence (AI) systems developed for triage in primary care and describe their characteristics, performance and clinical applicability. Methods A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, MEDLINE (via Ovid), Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL (via EBSCOhost), IEEE Xplore and the ACM Digital Library were searched until March 14th 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on system characteristics, triage function, performance, validation, safety, equity and implementation. Each system was charted by triage function and by whether it was patient-facing, clinician-facing or fully automated. Results Seventeen studies were included, published between 2013 and 2026 across 12 countries (14/17 high-income). Most were clinician-facing decision support (14/17), three had a patient-facing component and none were autonomous. Diagnostic or screening triage was the most common function (n = 7), followed by prioritisation (n = 4) and referral routing (n = 4). Only two performed urgency classification or self-triage. As a clinician aid, AI improved performance (fundus accuracy 82.8 % to 91.1 %; dermoscopy management sensitivity 72.9 % to 94.2 %), but standalone models sometimes fell below clinicians. Reported accuracy ranged from 41.2 % to 98.28 % and AUROC from 0.65 to 0.90, on heterogeneous outcomes. Validation was mostly internal (11/17), external in four. None reported a prospective randomised comparison or measured patient outcomes. Conclusion AI triage in primary care is concentrated on clinician-facing diagnostic and referral tasks and is most valuable for augmenting clinician workflows, particularly non-specialists. The evidence base remains immature, constrained by internal validation, unreliable reference standards, sparse equity assessment and absent prospective outcome data. Future work should prioritise prospective, outcome-anchored evaluation, with attention to safety and equity.

title: An unusual Case of p63/p40 Negative Myoepithelial cell-Rich Parotid Pleomorphic Adenoma.
abstract: Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common benign salivary gland neoplasm; however, myoepithelial-rich variants with unusual immunophenotypes are rare and pose diagnostic challenges. We report a myoepithelial-rich pleomorphic adenoma of the parotid gland in a 23-year-old male presenting with a slowly enlarging, painless infraauricular swelling. Grossly, the lesion was well-circumscribed and encapsulated. Histopathology revealed predominantly spindle, oval, and plasmacytoid myoepithelial cells embedded in densely hyalinized fibromyxoid stroma, with sparse ductal structures. The paucity of ducts and prominent myoepithelial proliferation closely mimicked myoepithelioma. Immunohistochemically, tumor cells showed diffuse expression of S100, pan-cytokeratin, and high-molecular-weight cytokeratin, supporting epithelial and myoepithelial differentiation. EMA and CD117 selectively highlighted the sparse ductal structures, providing a crucial diagnostic clue. Notably, the tumor was completely negative for p40, p63, and smooth muscle actin, representing an unusual immunophenotype for pleomorphic adenoma. Despite the absence of conventional myoepithelial markers, integration of the subtle residual ductal morphology and complementary immunoprofile established the diagnosis of myoepithelial-rich pleomorphic adenoma, excluding myoepithelioma and other salivary gland neoplasms. The patient recovered uneventfully after surgery and remained recurrence-free at six months. This case expands the immunohistochemical spectrum of pleomorphic adenoma and highlights that the absence of p40 and p63 expression should not preclude its diagnosis. Comprehensive immunohistochemical assessment, interpreted alongside meticulous histomorphological evaluation, is essential to avoid diagnostic pitfalls in these uncommon tumors.

title: Can radiological parameters predict failure of fixation in distal radius fractures treated with a volar locking plate?
abstract: Introduction Fractures of the distal radius are common, and volar locking plates are the most utilized fixation method. Failure of fixation, defined as post-operative fracture collapse leading to loss of reduction and/or screw penetration, is an undesirable outcome. We aimed to demonstrate whether preoperative and intraoperative radiographic parameters are associated with subsequent failure of fixation in order to produce a model that may be able to predict failure. Methods A retrospective case-control study of 23 cases of failure of fixation matched to controls from the same cohort by age, sex, and AO classification in a 3:1 ratio. Nine initial injury and 13 intraoperative radiological parameters were evaluated, and multi-variate regression analysis models were analysed to assess if they could reliably predict failure. Results A total of 92 patients were analysed (23 cases, 69 controls). Size of intraarticular gap was the only preoperative parameter to be associated failure with every 0.47 mm increase in fracture gap resulting in a 1.6 increase of odds ratio of failure. Based on intraoperative radiological parameters, three factors were associated with failure: dorsal capitate translation, intraarticular gap and step. Models based on these parameters do not accurately predict failure, however, models based on intraoperative factors are associated with risk of failure with high specificity but low sensitivity. Conclusion We conclude that the severity of the injury is less importantly associated with failure of fixation, whereas the quality of the surgical fixation and specifically the accuracy of the reduction are more important.

Fractures of the distal radius are common, and volar locking plates are the most utilized fixation method. Failure of fixation, defined as post-operative fracture collapse leading to loss of reduction and/or screw penetration, is an undesirable outcome. We aimed to demonstrate whether preoperative and intraoperative radiographic parameters are associated with subsequent failure of fixation in order to produce a model that may be able to predict failure.

Methods

A retrospective case-control study of 23 cases of failure of fixation matched to controls from the same cohort by age, sex, and AO classification in a 3:1 ratio. Nine initial injury and 13 intraoperative radiological parameters were evaluated, and multi-variate regression analysis models were analysed to assess if they could reliably predict failure.

Results

A total of 92 patients were analysed (23 cases, 69 controls). Size of intraarticular gap was the only preoperative parameter to be associated failure with every 0.47 mm increase in fracture gap resulting in a 1.6 increase of odds ratio of failure. Based on intraoperative radiological parameters, three factors were associated with failure: dorsal capitate translation, intraarticular gap and step. Models based on these parameters do not accurately predict failure, however, models based on intraoperative factors are associated with risk of failure with high specificity but low sensitivity.

Conclusion

We conclude that the severity of the injury is less importantly associated with failure of fixation, whereas the quality of the surgical fixation and specifically the accuracy of the reduction are more important.

title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

title: Assessing the incidence of retinal hemorrhage in pediatric patients following COVID-19 vaccination.
abstract: Background Retinal hemorrhages (RHs) are a cardinal finding in abusive head trauma (AHT) for which a broad differential diagnosis is appropriate to consider. The frequency of COVID-19 vaccination and reports of subsequent ocular manifestations have led to the consideration of whether COVID-19 vaccination should be included in the RH differential. This study aimed to investigate the frequency of RH following COVID-19 vaccination in children. Methods In this single-center, retrospective, observational cohort study, we reviewed the medical records of children ≤8 years of age who received a COVID-19 vaccine from July 1, 2020, to July 1, 2024, and underwent a fundus examination within 21 days of vaccination. The main outcome measure was incidence and characteristics of RH on fundus examination. Results Of 17,926 children vaccinated during this period, 203 subjects met inclusion criteria and underwent 212 unique examinations, with mean age of 4.56 years (0-8) at the time of first examination. Twenty examinations were also in the setting of prior COVID-19 infection. No examinations revealed RH. Based on Hanley's rule of zero incidence, the 95th percentile upper limit of incidence of RH after COVID-19 vaccination is 4.11% at 7 days, 2.04% at 14 days, and 1.42% at 21 days following vaccination. Conclusions RHs were not seen in any children within 21 days of COVID-19 vaccination. This suggests that RH is rare following COVID-19 vaccination and perhaps of little relevance to the differential diagnosis of RH in the evaluation for AHT.

title: Intraoperative and radiographic indicators of extraocular muscle aberrancy in syndromic craniosynostosis.
abstract: Background Strabismus is common in syndromic craniosynostosis, often attributed to abnormal extraocular muscle (EOM) trajectory, and orbital anatomy. Absent EOMs have been reported, but the spectrum of primary dysgenesis remains poorly understood. The purpose of this study was to characterize the range of EOM dysgenesis in a large cohort that had undergone strabismus surgery. Methods The medical records of patients with syndromic craniosynostosis treated at Boston Children's Hospital (2010-2023) were reviewed retrospectively to identify all cases with neuroimaging and history of strabismus surgery. Genetic testing results and EOM abnormalities noted on neuroimaging or during surgery were recorded. Imaging was reviewed to determine presence of each EOM. Superior oblique muscle (SO) size was classified as "normal" if its transverse diameter was at least one-half that of the adjacent medial rectus muscle. Results A total of 47 patients with syndromic craniosynostosis had undergone strabismus surgery, of whom 43 had available neuroimaging. Syndromic associations were as follows: 21 patients with Apert, 10 with Crouzon, 6 with Pfeiffer, 5 with Saethre-Chotzen, and 1 with Muenke. Rectus and inferior oblique muscles were universally present. SO size was normal in only 15 of 86 eyes (17%). EOM aberrancies were noted intraoperatively in 15 of 43 operative cases (35%), including diaphanous insertions, bifid or fused rectus muscles, and posterior inferior oblique insertions. Results of genetic testing were available for 26 patients, 24 of whom had FGFR2 mutations, including all 10 (of 15) patients with intraoperatively noted EOM aberrancies who underwent genetic testing. Conclusions In this cohort with syndromic craniosynostosis, thin-section or high-resolution orbital imaging demonstrated presence of all rectus muscles even when insertions were diaphanous. The SO was hypoplastic in 83%. Aberrancies noted intraoperatively in 35% likely underestimate the true incidence, because evaluation was limited to muscles targeted for surgery.

title: Abnormal left ventricular mass as a prognostic marker for outcomes in infants and children with cirrhosis.
abstract: Background/aims Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM), a clinically consequential comorbidity of cirrhosis, remains undefined and underappreciated in children. This study aimed to characterize myocardial structural, functional, morphometric, and histopathologic features in pediatric cirrhosis and objectively derive a reliable echocardiographic (2DE) metric to predict perioperative adverse events, including mortality. Methods 2DE, morphometry, histopathology, and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) were compared between children with (n=226) and without (n=160) cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation (LT) over 2011-2021. Discriminatory performance of left ventricular mass index (height) 2.7 (LVMI g/m 2.7 ) for predicting waitlist decompensation, composite serious adverse events post liver transplant and mortality was assessed using ROC analysis, with AUCs and optimal thresholds compared against PELD-Cr/MELD scores. Results LV mass was significantly higher in children with cirrhosis on 2DE and necropsy specimens compared to non-cirrhotic controls, with ∼25% demonstrating LV hypertrophy, with OR of 6.9 [CI 3,16], p< 0.0001. In the cirrhotic cohort, LVMI correlated with vasoactive needs under stress of LT (p <0.001) and was significantly higher in patients with WLD, CSAE, and non-survivors. In cirrhosis, LVMI values ≥ 88 g/m 2.7 , ≥ 91 g/m 2.7, and ≥ 95 g/m 2.7 were independently associated with WLD, CSAE, and mortality, when adjusting for PELD-Cr/MELD, bilirubin, and INR (p <0.01). Combining LVMI + PELD-Cr/MELD significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD in discriminating both WLD and CSAE, whereas LVMI alone significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD for CSAE and was comparable for WLD. All three models performed comparably in discriminating death. Conclusion LVMI is a strong predictor of morbidity and mortality, serving as a prognostic marker in children with cirrhosis. Incorporating LVMI into PELD-Cr/MELD may enhance risk stratification and organ allocation.

title: The Prognostic Value of Entropy from T1 Mapping in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
abstract: Background The prognostic value of left ventricular (LV) entropy from T1 mapping in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains unexplored. Study design and methods This prospective study enrolled patients with PAH who underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) within 72h of right heart catheterization (RHC). Myocardial native T1, extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and entropy were calculated in mid-ventricular short-axis slice. The primary endpoint was defined as all-cause mortality or lung transplantation. Outcomes were further analyzed across groups stratified by survival status using Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Results A total of 312 patients were analyzed over a median follow-up of 36.10 months, with 59 deaths. Elevated LV entropy was positively correlated with log-transformed NT-proBNP, right ventricular (RV) end-systolic, end-diastolic volume indices, LV native T1 and ECV, and inversely correlated with RV ejection fraction (all P < 0.01). LV entropy did not differ significantly across etiological subgroups, whereas LV entropy without IPs was higher in congenital heart disease-associated PAH. Both LV entropy ≥8.60 and LV entropy without IPs ≥8.30 independently predicted all-cause mortality (HR, 2.207; 95% CI, 1.324-3.678; P = 0.002; and HR, 2.357; 95% CI, 1.405-3.955; P = 0.001, respectively) and were associated with reduced survival (both log-rank P < 0.005). Adding LV entropy improved ESC models (χ²: 55.79 to 60.61, C-statistic: 0.782 to 0.801) and ESC-CMR models (χ²: 35.31 to 41.77, C-statistic: 0.805 to 0.813). Conclusions Elevated LV entropy was related to disease severity, RV dysfunction, and adverse clinical outcomes, and served as an independent predictor of all-cause mortality in patients with PAH. Registration URL: https://www. Clinicaltrials gov; Unique identifier: ChiCTR1800019314 and ChiCTR1900025518.

title: Automatic 3D TOF-MRA Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation using SAM-Guided Multi-View Decoding Network.
abstract: Background Deep learning-based aneurysm segmentation using 3D time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography (TOF-MRA) offers promising non-invasive screening, but its accuracy and generalizability remain limited. Purpose To develop a deep learning model for intracranial aneurysm detection and segmentation on MRA, and evaluate its multicenter performance against the digital subtraction angiography (DSA) gold standard and radiologists of varying experience. Materials and methods MRA images from patients suspected of harboring unruptured intracranial aneurysms were retrospectively collected from Jinhua Municipal Central Hospital for model development. An external test set, with DSA as the reference standard, was gathered from Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. Manual segmentation of cerebral arteries and aneurysms was performed using 3D-Slicer software. Performance was evaluated via Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), sensitivity, and F1-score, and compared against independent clinical evaluations from radiologists with different experience levels. Results The internal dataset comprised 1,560 patients (1,554 aneurysms), including 421 patients (522 aneurysms) for testing. The external test set included 208 patients (224 aneurysms). On the internal test set, the model achieved a lesion-level sensitivity of 86.0% (95% CI: 82.8 - 88.7), a precision of 87.4% (95% CI: 84.2, 90.0), and a DSC of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.84, 0.90). On the independent external test set, the model demonstrated robust generalizability with a sensitivity of 83.4% (95% CI: 75.9, 88.0) and a DSC of 0.84 (95% CI: 0.79, 0.87). The model achieved an overall detection F1-score of 86.7, significantly outperforming junior radiologists (P <.001) and was comparable to mid-level radiologists (P >.05), with an average processing time of approximately 72seconds per exam. Conclusion The proposed deep learning model demonstrated robust multicenter performance for intracranial aneurysm detection and segmentation. Achieving diagnostic accuracy comparable to mid-level radiologists, it holds potential as an efficient assistive tool for MRA interpretation in clinical workflows.

title: Predictive Modeling of Clinically Apparent Shoulder Periprosthetic Joint Infection (PJI).
abstract: Introduction The first International Consensus Meeting (ICM) definition of shoulder periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) introduced a tiered framework of PJI categories based on weighting of minor criteria for those cases not having major criteria of Definite infection. The selection of minor criteria and weightings was based on expert opinion and limited available evidence. The purpose of this study was to use prospective, multicenter data to develop a predictive model for clinically apparent shoulder PJI to inform a more evidence-based understanding of minor criteria and PJI categories. Methods Prospective data were collected on 861 consecutive revision shoulder arthroplasty cases within the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) Revision Shoulder Arthroplasty and PJI Multicenter Research Group. Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the prosthesis and intra-articular purulence were identified as pathognomonic indicators of infection (major criteria) and used as the primary outcome for multivariable analysis. Logistic regression modeling was performed, with model specification guided by information criteria. Variable selection emphasized optimal model fit while balancing complexity, focusing on: (1) markers of host inflammatory response, (2) universally available and commonly utilized diagnostic tests, (3) minimizing the total number of variables, and (4) preserving model usability despite missing data. Results Among 861 cases, 97 shoulders (11%) met the outcome of interest (sinus tract or intra-articular purulence). The final model incorporated seven variables spanning clinical findings, laboratory values, imaging, intraoperative assessment, and microbiology. These variables were erythema, unexpected wound drainage, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) or C-reactive protein (CRP), radiographic humeral osteolysis, synovial neutrophils ≥70% or positive frozen section (≥5 polymorphonuclear cells in ≥5 high-powered fields), intraoperative humeral loosening, and ≥2 positive cultures with the same organism. The apparent concordance statistic in the development cohort was 0.90 (95% CI 0.87-0.94). A nomogram was subsequently developed to estimate the probability of PJI, defined by the presence of a sinus tract or intra-articular purulence. Conclusion Using prospective, multicenter data, this study proposes a seven-factor nomogram to estimate the probability of clinically apparent shoulder PJI. The model showed strong apparent discrimination for clinically apparent infection in the development cohort. External validation will be necessary to confirm performance, and consensus will be required to establish weighting and diagnostic thresholds for tiers of non-definite shoulder PJI.

title: Artificial intelligence-supported diabetic retinopathy screening in Tanzania: a randomised controlled trial.
abstract: Background Non-attendance after referral from screening is one of the major challenges for diabetic retinopathy screening programmes in Africa. Artificial intelligence (AI) systems for the identification of diabetic retinopathy can provide point-of-screening results and therefore enable immediate counselling. We aimed to investigate whether AI-supported diabetic retinopathy screening, with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling, increased the proportion of people with true referable diabetic retinopathy who attended the central ophthalmology referral clinic when compared with standard diabetic retinopathy screening with deferred human grading and telephone counselling. Methods This two-arm, parallel-group, individually randomised controlled trial was conducted at non-communicable disease or diabetic clinics in 24 hospitals in the Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions of Tanzania. Eligible participants (aged ≥18 years) had diabetes and attended diabetic retinopathy screening. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either AI-supported diabetic retinopathy screening with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling (the AI-intervention group) or standard-of-care diabetic retinopathy screening with deferred human retinal image assessment and telephone counselling (the standard-of-care group). Participants had retinal photographs taken of both eyes. Images from the AI-intervention group were submitted to the AI software, and these participants were given their screening result (non-referable, referable, or ungradable) plus face-to-face counselling before leaving the photography room, with a referral to the central ophthalmology clinic if the AI output was referable or ungradable. Participants in the standard-of-care group received their screening result, along with appropriate counselling, by telephone a few weeks later. The primary outcome was attendance at the central ophthalmology clinic within 8 weeks of screening among participants classified by masked UK-certified graders as having true referable diabetic retinopathy. This trial was registered with the ISRCTN Registry, ISRCTN18317152, and is complete. Findings Between March 8, 2023, and Aug 31, 2024, 2439 participants were assessed for eligibility and 2378 were enrolled, of whom 1192 were randomly assigned to the AI-intervention group and 1186 to the standard-of-care group. 904 participants had true referable diabetic retinopathy, comprising 437 in the AI-intervention group and 467 in the standard-of-care group. Of the participants in the AI-intervention group, 157 (35·9%) of 437 attended the central ophthalmology clinic within 8 weeks, compared with 85 (18·2%) of 467 in the standard-of-care group, an absolute difference of 17·7 percentage points (95% CI 12·0-23·4; odds ratio 2·52 [95% CI 1·86-3·42]; p<0·0001). Interpretation AI-supported screening, with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling, increased the proportion of people with true referable diabetic retinopathy that attended the central ophthalmology clinic after screening compared with the standard of care in Tanzania. Such AI-enabled screening pathways have the potential to improve diabetic retinopathy screening programmes in Africa. title: Performance uncertainty in medical image analysis: A large-scale investigation of confidence intervals.
abstract: Performance uncertainty quantification is essential for reliable validation and eventual clinical translation of medical imaging artificial intelligence (AI). Confidence intervals (CIs) play a central role in this process by indicating how precise a reported performance estimate is. Yet, due to the limited amount of work examining CI behavior in medical imaging, the community remains largely unaware of how many diverse CI methods exist and how they behave in specific settings. The purpose of this study is to close this gap. To this end, we conducted a large-scale empirical analysis across a total of 24 segmentation and classification tasks, using 19 trained models per task group, a broad spectrum of commonly used performance metrics, multiple aggregation strategies, and several widely adopted CI methods. Reliability (coverage) and precision (width) of each CI method were estimated across all settings to characterize their dependence on study characteristics. Our analysis revealed five principal findings: (1) the sample size required for reliable CIs varies from a few dozens to several thousands of cases depending on study parameters; (2) CI behavior is strongly affected by the choice of performance metric; (3) aggregation strategy substantially influences the reliability of CIs, e.g. they require more observations for macro than for micro; (4) the machine learning problem (segmentation versus classification) modulates these effects; (5) different CI methods are not equally reliable and precise depending on the use case. Finally, we derived practical implications of this study in the form of a decision tree which shall prove useful to the community. This paves the way for future consensus guidelines on reporting performance uncertainty.

title: Meningioma in the modern era: Updates in stratification and therapeutic approaches.
abstract: Meningioma is the most common primary intracranial tumor in adults. Most meningiomas have an indolent growth pattern, but some can grow quickly. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification system is the gold standard for tumor grading and relies predominantly on histopathology and limited molecular alterations. It is increasingly recognized that the variability in tumor behaviour is incompletely captured using traditional systems. Contemporary advances have expanded tumor stratification beyond starting WHO grading, providing a more comprehensive framework for understanding tumor biology. Molecular profiling has identified independent biological classification systems and molecular signatures that capture important prognostic information beyond histopathology. Magnetic resonance imaging-based analyses and radiomics have enabled non-invasive characterization of tumor phenotype and growth potential. Therapeutically, surgical resection and radiation therapy remain the foundation of management, with evolving paradigms emphasizing maximal safe resection and risk-adapted radiotherapy strategies informed by integrated tumor characteristics. Systemic therapies have historically shown limited efficacy; however, recent efforts are shifting toward biomarker-driven, precision approaches guided by molecular alterations. Future directions focus on integrating multimodal data into unified, clinically actionable models that more accurately predict recurrence, progression, and treatment response. Such approaches aim to move beyond parallel classification systems toward individualized management strategies, ultimately advancing meningioma care into a precision-based paradigm.

title: Investigation of CardioFreeze Motion Correction for Cardiac PET/CT.
abstract: Background Cardiac imaging with positron emission tomography and computed tomography (PET/CT) is a principal technique in the diagnosis and prognostication of coronary artery disease. PET/CT image quality can be negatively impacted by patient, cardiac, and respiratory motion. Methods We evaluated images from 102 patients clinically referred for cardiac rest/stress Rb-82 PET/CT myocardial perfusion imaging. Patient images were processed with a prototype data-driven motion detection algorithm and stratified by motion severity. Images were subjected to cardiac (CS) or cardiac and respiratory (CD) motion correction via a novel reconstruction tool. Validated image quality markers including target-to-background ratio (TBR) were assessed between corrected and non-corrected images and analyzed via student's t-tests. Results The motion detection algorithm identified 36 (35.3%) patients with significant motion. Image processing via CS yielded a statistically significant increase in mean image contrast (TBR 3.65±0.07, p<0.01) and intensified when respiratory motion correction was applied (3.78±0.07, p<0.005). Motion correction is more effective when applied to images containing greater motion, improving mean TBR by 3% (p<0.05) in non-motion scans but >10% (p<0.01) in significant motion cases. Three months post-imaging, 18 patients underwent clinically indicated coronary angiography: seven patients demonstrated significant motion, and CD motion correction improved their image quality to that of patients with no motion. Conclusions Over 1/3 of patients undergoing cardiac PET/CT have detectible motion leading to potential artifacts with clinical significance. Cardiac and respiratory motion correction improves image quality and may improve diagnostic accuracy, particularly when respiratory motion is severe. Further studies are critical to investigate the clinical impacts of improved image quality.

title: Multicenter Evaluation of a Deep Learning Model for Automatic Contouring of Cardiac Substructures in Adults.
abstract: Purpose Efficient delineation of cardiac substructures is essential for assessing radiation-induced cardiac toxicity in thoracic radiotherapy. We clinically evaluated a deep learning model designed for automated segmentation of these structures. Methods and materials The model built in collaboration with XXX (XXX) generated 21 cardiac substructures (whole heart, chambers, coronary arteries, valves, and great vessels). Five radiation oncologists rated raw contours on thirty contrast-enhanced CTs from two institutions using a 4-point Likert scale (3 = no correction, 2 = minor/moderate correction, 1 = major correction, 0 = not performed) and applied corrections when needed. Dice Similarity Coefficients (DSC) and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distances (HD95) were computed to compare model versus reference contours, clinician-corrected versus reference contours, and model versus STAPLE contours. Results Of 630 structures, 93.8% were scored either 3 or ≥2, and 6.2% received 1 by at least one clinician. For the coronary arteries (210 structures), 88.5% were scored either 3 or ≥ 2. Contour generation took approximately 1 min, with a median review and correction time of 7.0 min per CT (IQR, 5.8-9.8). The median DSC between the model and reference contours was 1.0 across all structures, while it ranged from 0.92 to 1.0 for clinician-corrected versus reference contours. Overall, HD95 was below 5 mm, for both clinicians versus reference and model versus STAPLE. Conclusions The deep learning model provided satisfactory segmentation of cardiac substructures on contrast-enhanced CT, including coronary arteries. Its integration into a widely adopted treatment planning system lays the foundation for broad clinical implementation.

title: Inadvertent Coronary Sinus Cannulation During Central Venous Catheter Placement in a Liver Transplant Recipient with Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava: A Case Report.
abstract: Persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) is the most common thoracic venous anomaly and is usually asymptomatic. Central venous catheterization through a PLSVC can be challenging, and inadvertent advancement of catheters into the coronary sinus may result in arrhythmias, perforation, thrombosis, or inaccurate hemodynamic measurements. We report a case of coronary sinus cannulation by a left internal jugular dialysis catheter in a liver transplant recipient with previously unrecognized PLSVC. Initial chest radiography suggested catheter termination within a duplicated left superior vena cava; however, intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) demonstrated the catheter tip within the coronary sinus. The catheter was withdrawn under direct echocardiographic guidance, avoiding potential complications. This case highlights the utility of intraoperative TEE for definitive localization of central venous catheters in patients with anomalous thoracic venous anatomy.

title: Automated Segmentation of Intrinsic Foot Muscles in Ultrasound Using Deep Neural Networks: Development and Validation Study.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate the first automated deep-learning image-processing framework for pixel-level segmentation of the plantar intrinsic foot muscles (PIMs) in ultrasound (US) images. This approach supports objective and reproducible US-based muscle segmentation from conventional B-mode images. Methods US images of four PIMs (abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis (FDB), quadratus plantae [QP] and abductor digiti minimi) were collected from 200 healthy participants (n = 1099 images). Manual segmentations were used as ground truth. Three deep neural network architectures (U-Net, Feature Pyramid Network [FPN] and DeepLabV3+) with a Mix Transformer backbone were trained and evaluated. Model performance was assessed using the Intersection over Union (IoU) and Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), two complementary pixel-level segmentation metrics. Agreement with manual measurements was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), mean difference and standard error of measurement. Results All models demonstrated excellent segmentation performance, with mean IoU values ≥0.90 and mean DSC values ≥0.95 across all muscles. The highest accuracy was observed for the FDB (IoU = 0.95; DSC = 0.97), while QP showed slightly lower performance (IoU = 0.90; DSC = 0.95). FPN and DeepLabV3+ exhibited greater stability (SD: ±0.02-0.03) compared to U-Net (up to ±0.08). Agreement with manual segmentation was high for cross-sectional area (ICC: 0.836-0.960) and moderate-to-high for border length (ICC: 0.705-0.944), with minimal systematic bias. Mean model inference time was under 0.01 s per image, reflecting forward-pass model inference only and excluding image loading, resizing and post-processing. Conclusion This study presents the first automated segmentation framework for the PIMs in US. Built on established segmentation architectures with a Mix Transformer backbone, it enables accurate and reliable pixel-level segmentation in under 0.01 s per image; its novelty lies in extending automated musculoskeletal US analysis to this previously unaddressed muscle group. By automating tissue boundary detection at the pixel level, this framework advances US imaging beyond conventional manual measurement, enabling objective and scalable musculoskeletal assessment with reduced operator dependence at the segmentation stage. These findings establish the feasibility of accurate and reproducible PIM segmentation in healthy adults and provide the necessary foundation for subsequent validation in clinical populations.

title: X-ray µ-CT contrast agents employing highly-concentrated low-viscosity layered double hydroxide nanoparticles for high-resolution imaging of vasculature.
abstract: Contrast agents capable of being injected and cured in situ within the vasculature are required for angiography based on X-ray microcomputed tomography (µ-CT) for pathophysiology of biopsies or postmortem. In this study, we developed a contrast agent based on highly-concentrated methanolic dispersion of NiAl-type layered double hydroxide nanoparticles (NiAl-LDH NPs) for X-ray µ-CT imaging of vasculature. We optimized the synthesis conditions of the constituent NiAl-LDH NPs, with particular attention to drying conditions and dispersion media selection. The formulated contrast agent achieved a particle concentration >30 wt%, a curing time of ∼30 min, and low viscosity (<100 mPa s). These properties enabled successful perfusion into small vessels and capillaries giving excellent X-ray attenuation following setting without tissue maceration. Consequently, this enabled reliable vessel identification and segmentation using simple intensity-based approaches giving a robust approach to accelerated tissue screening.

title: Practice Variability in Anorectal Malformations Management across Europe: A TEPS-EUPSA Survey with Analysis of Center Volume Effects.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate management strategies for anorectal malformations (ARMs) across Europe and assess the impact of institutional case volume on clinical decision-making.A cross-sectional online survey developed within the Trainees in European Pediatric Surgery (TEPS) and endorsed by the European Paediatric Surgeons' Association (EUPSA) Network Office was distributed among pediatric surgeons involved in ARM care. The questionnaire addressed diagnostic workup, surgical management, perioperative care, and long-term follow-up. European responses were analyzed and compared by institutional case volume.A total of 94 responses from 21 countries were analyzed. Substantial variability was observed across all domains of care. Ultrasound-based screening and invertogram were widely used, whereas high-pressure distal colostography was variably applied. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and vaginoscopy were used more selectively. Primary neonatal repair in cases with the rectum located <1 cm from the perineal skin was commonly performed, and staged reconstruction was most frequently undertaken at 3 to 6 months. Non-divided stomas were more frequently used in high-volume centers ( p = 0.002), with increasing center volume associated with higher odds of their use (odds ratio [OR] 2.98, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.51-5.87, p = 0.002). Routine anal dilations were reported by 44.7% of respondents and were less common in high-volume centers ( p = 0.005); increasing volume was associated with lower odds of routine dilation (OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.20-0.72, p = 0.003).ARM management across Europe remains highly variable. Institutional case volume is associated with practice differences, particularly in stoma configuration and postoperative dilation strategies.

title: Interstitial Lung Abnormalities: A Multidisciplinary Narrative Review.
abstract: Abstract Interstitial lung abnormalities (ILAs) is an umbrella term used to describe a spectrum of computed tomography (CT)-detected lung abnormalities that may reflect interstitial lung disease (ILD). Initially perceived as a niche topic-and often underreported in clinical practice-ILAs have gained increasing attention in recent years, given growing evidence of their association with several adverse outcomes, including increased all-cause, respiratory, and cancer-related mortality. Over time, efforts have been made to standardize the definition, classification, and management of ILAs. The recent American Thoracic Society clinical statement has reshaped the definition of ILAs proposed by the Fleischner Society in 2020, introducing substantial changes to the populations in whom ILAs may be identified and proposing new boundaries to distinguish ILAs from ILD. Nevertheless, several key aspects remain debated, and growing efforts are being made to balance the opportunity for early ILD diagnosis against the risk of unnecessary burden on patients and healthcare systems. This is particularly relevant given the increasing number of CT examinations performed in the general population, as well as in patients at increased risk of ILD, such as those with connective tissue disease, and considering the substantial number of examinations related to expanding implementation of lung cancer screening. In this narrative review, we focus on the definition, implications, and management of ILAs, integrating pulmonology, radiology, and pathology perspectives on the strengths and limitations of current approaches.

title: ReCo-Diff: residual-conditioned deterministic sampling for cold diffusion in sparse-view CT.
abstract: Objective Sparse-view computed tomography (CT) reduces radiation dose and acquisition time but introduces structured streak artifacts that make reconstruction severely ill-posed. Cold-diffusion approaches can model such deterministic degradation processes, but existing sampling strategies may rely on scalar similarity criteria and predefined thresholds to trigger sample-adaptive resets of the degradation-level trajectory. We aim to replace this threshold-based sampling control with spatially resolved residual conditioning. Approach We propose ReCo-Diff, a residual-conditioned cold-diffusion framework for sparse-view CT reconstruction. At each reverse step, a zero-residual baseline prediction is re-degraded using the CT degradation operator, and the resulting signed image-domain re-degradation discrepancy is used as a spatial conditioning map for a second restoration pass. ReCo-Diff does not require an adaptive reset during residual-conditioned sampling and instead follows a predetermined degradation schedule. A one-time level transition is additionally used for highly sparse inputs. The method was evaluated on the AAPM Low-Dose CT dataset under 18-, 36-, and 72-view settings using a patient-wise split with one held-out test volume. Main results ReCo-Diff achieved PSNR values of 38.54, 42.57, and 46.98 dB at 18, 36, and 72 views, respectively. At 18 views, matched-computation analysis showed that ReCo-Diff achieved 38.54 dB compared with 38.25 dB for a two-pass zero-residual control under the same 18-NFE budget. A spatially shifted-residual control achieved 37.65 dB, indicating that effective residual conditioning benefits from spatial correspondence with the current degraded state. Significance. ReCo-Diff replaces adaptive trajectory control with step-wise spatial residual conditioning in deterministic cold diffusion. Matched-computation analysis shows that the reconstruction benefit depends on spatially aligned residual information rather than on the additional network evaluation alone. The proposed strategy provides an alternative approach to controlling error propagation under a predetermined degradation schedule without relying on sample-adaptive reset decisions.

title: Integrating radiomic features and spatial semantic features from multiparametric MRI for IDH genotyping in glioma.
abstract: Gliomas, one of the most prevalent primary tumors of the central nervous system, have IDH molecular subtypes that are strongly linked to patient survival, prognosis, and treatment plans. However, there are currently few noninvasive preoperative prediction techniques, and postoperative pathology and genetic testing are the main approaches used to assess IDH status. Radiomics features can quantitatively characterize intratumoral heterogeneity, whereas spatial semantic features may provide additional information related to tumor location and macroscopic growth patterns. When it comes to characteristics like glioma invasiveness, growth patterns, and angiogenesis, spatial semantic features can enhance radiomics features. In order to predict IDH molecular subtypes in gliomas, this study suggests a combined analytical approach that incorporates clinical data, spatial semantic features, and multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomic features. This technique uses the IBSI standard to extract radiomic data from raw multiparametric MRI images and combines morphological analysis, gradient statistics, and 3D geometric modeling to create spatial semantic information. To eliminate redundant features and account for multicollinearity, Pearson correlation analysis and the variance inflation factor were utilized. The best feature subset was then obtained through a multi-stage feature selection procedure that combined random forests (RFs), LASSO regression, and recursive feature elimination. Lastly, imaging characteristics and clinical data were combined using a RF model to identify IDH molecular subtypes in gliomas. According to experimental findings, the suggested model's area under the ROC curve (AUC) in a five-fold cross-validation was 96.08%. The model had the AUC of 95.62%, ACC of 91.67%, sensitivity of 88.89%, and specificity of 93.94% in the final test set. The limitations of radiomics in conveying tumor macroscopic development patterns and spatial invasion relationships can be somewhat compensated for by spatial semantic aspects, according to additional investigation. title: Structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders: an ESGE-ESHRE-IFFS international consensus†ǂ.
abstract: Study question How should the findings of diagnostic hysteroscopy in women with reproductive disorders be reported? Summary answer This collaborative document by the European Society for Gynaecological Endoscopy (ESGE), the ESHRE, and the International Federation of Fertility Societies (IFFS) provides the first detailed structured reporting template for diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders. What is known already Despite its widespread use in women with reproductive disorders, no standardized framework currently exists for reporting of hysteroscopic findings. This lack of uniformity may limit the utility of the procedure and contribute to substantial heterogeneity among operators and centers. As a result, the reproducibility of hysteroscopy is limited, making it difficult to conduct robust studies that define its prognostic value in specific patient subgroups. originalAbstract:
Study question

How should the findings of diagnostic hysteroscopy in women with reproductive disorders be reported?

Summary answer

This collaborative document by the European Society for Gynaecological Endoscopy (ESGE), the ESHRE, and the International Federation of Fertility Societies (IFFS) provides the first detailed structured reporting template for diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders.

What is known already

Despite its widespread use in women with reproductive disorders, no standardized framework currently exists for reporting of hysteroscopic findings. This lack of uniformity may limit the utility of the procedure and contribute to substantial heterogeneity among operators and centers. As a result, the reproducibility of hysteroscopy is limited, making it difficult to conduct robust studies that define its prognostic value in specific patient subgroups.

Study design, size, duration

A dedicated working group from ESGE, ESHRE, and IFFS collaborated to develop a consensus for comprehensive structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive problems.

Participants/materials, setting, methods

This consensus paper focuses on grouping diagnostic hysteroscopic findings, structuring their reporting, and adopting standardized terminology for women with reproductive disorders. The virtual Nominal Group Technique, a structured consensus-building method, was adopted to ensure equal contribution from all members in the development of the final consensus.

Main results and the role of chance

The document provides a structured reporting of hysteroscopic findings into five sections, each systematically capturing patient characteristics, procedural findings, and pathological observations as follows: patient's characteristics, and findings from the vagina, cervix, uterine cavity, endometrium, and tubal ostia.

Limitations, reasons for caution

The inclusion of a finding in this structured report is not a proof of its clinical significance, but it could be used as a validation tool for further research.

Wider implications of the findings

The standardized reporting of hysteroscopic findings promotes consistent data collection across centers and could help inform research and exchange of clinical experience, enhancing the value of hysteroscopy in fertility evaluation.

Funding

No external funding was received for the development of the consensus process or manuscript preparation.

Disclosures

All authors declare that they have no competing interests.

Trial registration number

N/A.

title: Long-term Outcomes in Previously Healthy non-HIV Individuals with Cryptococcal Meningitis Treated with Pulse-taper Corticosteroids for Post-infectious Inflammatory Syndrome.
abstract: Background Post-infectious inflammatory response syndrome (PIIRS) is an increasingly recognized complication of cryptococcal meningoencephalitis (CM) in non-HIV infected hosts with significant morbidity and mortality. Data describing long-term outcomes following immunomodulatory therapy are limited. Methods We conducted a prospective observational study of 15 immunocompetent adults with CM-PIIRS treated with a pulse corticosteroid taper (PCT) regimen. Performance status, neurocognitive, ophthalmologic, audiologic, and radiologic assessments were performed at greater than one year following CM diagnosis. Results After one year, performance status continued to improve from both baseline and the post-pulse periods. Neurocognitive testing revealed mild residual deficits, within the limits of normal, most prominently in information processing and psychomotor speed. Ocular abnormalities were frequent at baseline but showed substantial and sustained reductions following PCT, particularly in retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. Visual field deficits improved by 40% and remained stable thereafter. Evidence for changes in hearing sensitivity at post 1-year follow-up was mixed with 44.5% of ears meeting criteria for improvement, 11% for worsening, and 44.5% being stable. Radiologic abnormalities improved in 79% of patients, although intermittent inflammatory flares occurred during PCT but responded to dose escalation. A prolonged corticosteroid taper may be helpful, and MRI imaging can be used to evaluate response to taper. Conclusions In immunocompetent patients with CM-PIIRS, adjunctive corticosteroid therapy was associated with sustained improvement in neurologic, visual, and radiologic outcomes with mixed improvement in hearing after a year of therapy, with mild residual deficits.

We conducted a prospective observational study of 15 immunocompetent adults with CM-PIIRS treated with a pulse corticosteroid taper (PCT) regimen. Performance status, neurocognitive, ophthalmologic, audiologic, and radiologic assessments were performed at greater than one year following CM diagnosis.

Results

After one year, performance status continued to improve from both baseline and the post-pulse periods. Neurocognitive testing revealed mild residual deficits, within the limits of normal, most prominently in information processing and psychomotor speed. Ocular abnormalities were frequent at baseline but showed substantial and sustained reductions following PCT, particularly in retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. Visual field deficits improved by 40% and remained stable thereafter. Evidence for changes in hearing sensitivity at post 1-year follow-up was mixed with 44.5% of ears meeting criteria for improvement, 11% for worsening, and 44.5% being stable. Radiologic abnormalities improved in 79% of patients, although intermittent inflammatory flares occurred during PCT but responded to dose escalation. A prolonged corticosteroid taper may be helpful, and MRI imaging can be used to evaluate response to taper.

In immunocompetent patients with CM-PIIRS, adjunctive corticosteroid therapy was associated with sustained improvement in neurologic, visual, and radiologic outcomes with mixed improvement in hearing after a year of therapy, with mild residual deficits.

title: Catamenial haemolacria and ocular pain as rare manifestations of extra-pelvic endometriosis.
abstract: Ocular involvement in endometriosis is an exceptionally rare extrapelvic manifestation, typically presenting as catamenial haemorrhagia. We report the case of an adolescent girl who presented with recurrent eye bleeding and pain during her menstruation. A comprehensive physical examination and imaging, including orbital magnetic resonance imaging, were unremarkable. Hematologic and ophthalmological evaluations excluded coagulopathies and structural ocular pathologies. Given the cyclical pattern of her symptoms and the absence of other identifiable causes, a presumptive diagnosis of ocular endometriosis was made. The patient was treated with a combination of dienogest and ethinyl estradiol, leading to significant symptom improvement over a two-year follow-up period. Occasional minimal haemolacria persisted, but no further intervention was required. This case underscores the importance of considering endometriosis in the differential diagnosis of catamenial haemolacria, even in the absence of radiological confirmation. A multidisciplinary approach and individualized hormonal therapy can result in substantial symptom control and improved quality of life in affected patients with catamenial haemolacria.

title: Modified Sullivan-type segment III hepatojejunostomy for radiologically presumed unresectable hilar cholangiocarcinoma: a technical case report.
abstract: Hilar cholangiocarcinoma may present with advanced biliary obstruction requiring palliation. An 80-year-old frail woman with jaundice and severe pruritus had contrast-enhanced computed tomography findings radiologically consistent with Bismuth-Corlette type IV hilar cholangiocarcinoma. No tissue diagnosis was obtained. Cancer antigen 19-9, carcinoembryonic antigen, alkaline phosphatase, magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, and percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography were unavailable at the treating hospital and were not performed. Because referral and non-operative biliary drainage were not feasible and the patient requested active symptom-directed treatment, a modified Sullivan-type segment III hepatojejunostomy was performed. Operative time was 85 min and blood loss 100 ml. Pruritus resolved and bilirubin decreased from 191.78 to 127.81 μmol/l by postoperative Day 10. The patient died ~2 months later from disease progression. The procedure therefore provided short-term symptomatic improvement and partial biochemical improvement only, illustrating a potential palliative option when standard drainage modalities are inaccessible.

title: Primary Epstein-Barr virus-negative lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma of the supraglottic larynx mimicking nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a case report.
abstract: Lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma (LELC) of the larynx is exceptionally rare and can closely mimic undifferentiated nasopharyngeal carcinoma. A 78-year-old man presented with progressive dysphonia and dysphagia. Endoscopy and computed tomography showed a supraglottic lesion with bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy (cT2N2M0). Biopsy demonstrated poorly differentiated non-keratinizing carcinoma with dense lymphoid stroma and a Schmincke-type pattern. Tumor cells were positive for p40, p63, and pancytokeratins; Epstein-Barr virus testing was negative. After exclusion of a nasopharyngeal primary, the diagnosis of primary laryngeal LELC was established. Definitive cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy with intensity-modulated radiotherapy (70 Gy in 35 fractions) achieved complete clinical and radiological response at 12 months with preserved swallowing and phonatory function.

title: Documented Fracture-Healing Outcomes After Operative and Nonoperative Management of Closed Mid-Diaphyseal Humerus Fractures in Active-Duty Service Members.
abstract: Introduction Closed diaphyseal humerus fracture treatment is nuanced with regard to the selection of surgical candidates. Fracture union is crucial, with historical data suggesting rivaling union rates between operative and nonoperative treatment; however, recent literature suggests increased union rates with operative treatment. Although nonoperative treatment of most fracture patterns is supported by the literature, there remains an argument for operative treatment for select patient populations, especially when considering union rates. Evidence regarding fracture-healing outcomes in young active-duty populations remains limited. We sought to characterize documented fracture-healing outcomes after operative and nonoperative management of closed diaphyseal humerus fractures in active-duty service members and to evaluate completeness of healing-status ascertainment. Methods This study queried the Medical Assessment and Readiness System (MARS), Womack Army Medical Center, Fort Bragg, NC, which contains information from the Military Health System (MHS) care system. This study defined a retrospective cohort of patients diagnosed with closed diaphyseal humerus fractures (OTA/AO 12A/B/C), using International Classification of Diseases (9th and 10th revision) codes, sustained from January 2011 to December 2022. Treatment type, including operative or nonoperative, was identified. We excluded patients with open humerus fractures; proximal humerus fractures; distal humerus fractures; and those treated with external fixation. The primary outcome measure was a diagnosis of union or malunion/nonunion. Unadjusted comparisons between groups were conducted using likelihood ratio chi-square tests. Results The study population comprised 402 patients with closed humeral diaphyseal fractures; 314 (78.1%) were managed nonoperatively and 88 (21.9%) operatively. Fracture-healing status could be classified in 216 patients (53.7%), whereas 186 (46.3%) lacked sufficient documentation to determine the primary outcome. Outcome ascertainment was more complete after operative than nonoperative management (61/88 [69.3%] vs. 155/314 [49.4%]; P = .001). Among those with documented healing status, union occurred in 149 of 155 nonoperatively managed fractures (96.1%; 95% CI, 91.8%-98.6%) and 59 of 61 operatively managed fractures (96.7%; 95% CI, 88.7%-99.6%). Discussion Among active-duty service members with documented healing status after closed diaphyseal humerus fracture, observed union rates were high after both nonoperative and operative management. However, treatment was nonrandom, important fracture-specific treatment-selection variables were unavailable, and healing status was determined from available clinical documentation, recorded radiographic interpretations, diagnosis codes, and revision procedures rather than standardized radiographic adjudication. These limitations, together with incomplete and differential outcome ascertainment and few nonunion/malunion events, preclude estimation of a comparative treatment effect. The findings should therefore be interpreted descriptively rather than as evidence of equivalence between operative and nonoperative treatment.

title: Cardiovascular risk stratification using chest CT in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of incidentally detected coronary artery calcification (CAC) on routine chest computed tomography (CT) for cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM). Methods In this single-centre cross-sectional study, adult patients with IIM who underwent noncardiac, nongated high-resolution chest CT (HRCT) were included. CAC was visually categorized as absent, mild, moderate, or severe. Diagnostic performance for established coronary artery disease (CAD) and established cardiovascular (CV) events was assessed. Kaplan-Meier analyses evaluated CV death-free survival, and multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with CAC. A matched systemic sclerosis (SSc) cohort served as validation cohort. Results Among 234 patients with IIM (mean age 57.1±15.9 years; 70.1% female), CAC was present in 43.2%. Higher CAC thresholds showed greater specificity for established CAD and prior CV events, whereas lower thresholds were more sensitive. CAC was associated with reduced CV death-free survival (log-rank p = 0.0095), with a stepwise decline across CAC severity categories. Findings were similar in the matched SSc cohort. Increasing CAC burden was associated with older age, smoking, higher CV risk burden, interstitial lung disease, and higher disease activity. In adjusted analyses, high disease activity was independently associated with moderate CAC (OR 4.01, 95% CI 1.29-12.50), while a higher number of concomitant DMARDs was associated with severe CAC (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.27-5.11). Conclusion Incidentally detected CAC on routine chest CT provides diagnostic and prognostic information in IIM and may represent a pragmatic approach to improve cardiovascular risk stratification in this high-risk population.

title: Development of a Multivariable Prognostic Model for Risk Stratification in C1 Fractures.
abstract: Study design Retrospective analysis of adult patients with radiographically confirmed C1 fractures treated across a single healthcare system including multiple level 1 trauma centers and multiple community hospitals (2015-22). The primary outcome was instability. Peri-operative outcomes and complications were also considered. Objective To evaluate radiographic and clinical predictors of instability or surgical management in patients with C1 fractures and to develop a multivariable prognostic model. Summary of background data Determining instability in C1 fractures remains challenging. Traditional criteria rely heavily on radiographic displacement thresholds, which may not fully capture the multifactorial nature of atlas fracture instability. Methods Demographic, clinical, and radiographic variables were analyzed including lateral mass displacement, dens fracture, neurologic deficit, age, sex, and body mass index. Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression was used to adjust for confounders and identify factors significantly associated with instability/operative treatment. Receiver operating characteristic analysis assessed model discrimination. A point-based instability risk score was derived from model coefficients. Results In adjusted analysis of Two hundred and seventy-nine patients, Lateral mass displacement (OR 1.20 per mm, 95% CI 1.09-1.33, P<0.001), dens fracture (OR 2.67, 95% CI 1.35-5.38, P=0.0047), and neurologic deficit (OR 5.22, 95% CI 1.69-16.1, P=0.0047) were significantly associated with instability or surgical management. The traditional 7-mm displacement threshold performed poorly (AUC 0.64, P=0.012). The multivariable model demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.75. Based on the final multivariable regression model, a point-based instability risk score was derived to estimate patient-specific risk with good predictive accuracy. Conclusions Instability in C1 fractures was significantly associated with several factors including increasing lateral mass displacement, dens fracture, and neurologic deficit. These parameters outperformed legacy assessment tools based on radiographic measurement. Our prognostic utility demonstrated improved predictive performance and may assist clinicians in risk stratification and treatment decision-making.

title: Diagnosis and Management of HIV-Associated Colitis.
abstract: A 63-year-old male with a history of untreated HIV presented to the emergency room with acute on chronic watery diarrhea, weight loss, fatigue, fever and chills. His vital signs were within normal limits and his abdomen was soft, nondistended and tender to palpation in 4 quadrants without peritonitis. He did not have leukocytosis on presentation. CD4 count was 310. CT scan showed inflammatory changes in the rectum and sigmoid colon. Comprehensive infectious workup was negative for any pathogens including cytomegalovirus (CMV), cryptosporidium, chlamydia, gonorrhea, C. difficile, cryptococcus, tuberculosis (TB) and herpes simplex virus (HSV). Colonoscopy was performed and showed a continuous area of nonbleeding ulcerated mucosa in the rectum, sigmoid, descending and transverse colon (Fig. 1). Pancolonic biopsies revealed active colitis with focal areas of basal plasmacytosis and crypt branching in left colon, suggestive of acute on chronic colitis and possible ulcerative colitis (UC). Gastroenterology and infectious disease were consulted and patient was started on IV methylprednisolone for presumed UC flare. Over the next few weeks, the patient proceeded to develop melena as well as increased lower abdominal and pelvic pain with intermittent fevers despite IV steroid treatment. The patient was trialed on IV infliximab also without significant improvement. After several weeks of steroid and biologic treatment, he developed increased abdominal pain with tachycardia and hemodynamic instability. His examination was significant for peritonitis with abdominal distension concerning for fulminant colitis. Colorectal surgery was consulted and proceeded to do an emergent total abdominal colectomy and end ileostomy. Intraoperatively he was found to have a small anterior distal rectal perforation. The decision was made to drain this area widely with rectal drain and fecal diversion and start him on IV antibiotic therapy. His final pathology from the index operation showed ulceration and acute colitis. There was no chronic crypt architectural distortion such as crypt dropout, disarray, crypt branching or basal plasmacytosis that are often seen in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). There was also increased apoptotic bodies and mitoses that were not consistent with IBD. After reviewing the clinical presentation, his disease progression, and final pathology, the treating team diagnosed the patient with HIV-associated colitis.

title: Macular Laceration Following Intravitreal Injection in a Nanophthalmic Eye: Management with Pars Plana Vitrectomy.
abstract: Purpose To report a case of macular laceration following intravitreal injection in a nanophthalmic eye and its surgical management. Methods A nanophthalmic patient presented with visual decline after intravitreal bevacizumab injection. Multimodal imaging demonstrated a full-thickness macular defect, vitreous hemorrhage, and epiretinal membrane (ERM), consistent with suspected needle-induced injury. Following failed medical therapy, 27-gauge pars plana vitrectomy with internal limiting membrane peeling and gas tamponade was performed using modified sclerotomy placement. Results Surgery was successfully completed with treatment of an intraoperative peripheral retinal break. At 3.5 months, visual acuity improved from hand movements to 20/80. Optical coherence tomography confirmed ERM resolution, retinal reattachment, and restoration of macular architecture without cystoid macular edema or uveal effusion. Conclusion Macular laceration is a rare but potentially vision-threatening complication of intravitreal injection, with increased risk in anatomically crowded eyes such as nanophthalmos. Careful surgical planning allows successful vitrectomy with favorable anatomical and visual outcomes in this high-risk population.

title: Improved Visualization of Heart Valves With 4D-CT Using a Novel Motion Correction Algorithm.
abstract: Objective Motion artifacts remain a limitation of cardiac CT when assessing both native and prosthetic heart valves, particularly during phases of rapid motion. This may lead to reduced image quality, potentially impairing the evaluation of valvular movement and pathology. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether a novel reconstruction-based motion correction algorithm improves image quality and reduces motion artifacts of native and prosthetic heart valves compared with standard reconstructions in photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT). Materials and methods In this retrospective single-center study, 57 patients [21 women; median age, 71 (interquartile range, 57 to 78 y)] who underwent clinically indicated 4D cardiac CT for suspected native and prosthetic valvular disease were included. Images were acquired using retrospectively electrocardiography (ECG)-gated spiral dual-source PCD-CT without ECG-pulsing. Images were reconstructed in 10% steps throughout the RR-interval using both standard (TrueStack) and an otherwise identical reconstruction using the novel motion correction algorithm (ZeeFreePlus). Subjective image quality and motion artifacts were independently assessed by 2 blinded, experienced readers using a 4-point visual analog scale for 3 categories: valve frame/annulus, valve leaflets, and valvular pathology. Objective analysis included quantification of the volume of artifacts throughout the cardiac cycle. Results A total of 68 valves were evaluated, including 57 prosthetic valves (22 transcatheter aortic valve replacements and 19 surgical valves, 11 mitral valves, and 5 tricuspid valve interventions) and 11 native valves. Valvular pathology was present in 29 cases, with the most prevalent being hypoattenuated leaflet thickening in 14/29 (48%). Motion-corrected reconstructions significantly improved image quality and reduced motion artifacts across all cardiac phases and all categories (all, P<0.001). The largest improvements were observed during systole, particularly at 10% of the RR-interval, with significantly greater gains than during diastole (P<0.05). Improvements were consistent across aortic and atrioventricular prosthetic valves and translated into improved visualization of valvular pathology (P<0.001). Objective quantitative analysis corroborated the subjective image quality findings by demonstrating reductions in the volumes of motion-induced artifacts when using the algorithm (P<0.001). Conclusions A novel motion correction algorithm substantially reduced motion artifacts and improved image quality in both native and prosthetic heart valve imaging with PCD-CT, with the largest improvements in systole. These benefits resulted in enhanced visualization of valvular pathology, potentially reinforcing the growing clinical role of cardiac CT for the assessment of valve disease.

title: Anatomy of the Upper Lip and Nose Muscular Bundle Tendon and Its Application During Unilateral Cleft Lip Repair.
abstract: Background While several authors have previously described the anatomy of the nasolabial muscles in patients with unilateral cleft lip, some personal intraoperative findings may provide additional information on this topic. The aim of this study is to describe the anatomy and histopathology of the tendon of the upper lip and nose muscle bundle on the cleft side and the role of myrtiform muscles during primary repair of the unilateral cleft lip. Methods The anatomy of this structure has been described during primary cleft lip repair, and small pieces of the muscle and tendon of the upper lip muscular bundle were excised and embedded in paraffin for histopathologic study. In addition, a retrospective cross-sectional study was performed to evaluate the utility of this anatomic structure in cleft lip and nose repair. The outcomes were anthropometric measurements of the repaired lip and nose at the age of 5 years. Results The anatomic descriptions during cleft lip repair and the histopathologic study confirm the existence of this tendon structure in all the studied cases. A well-defined tendon was detected at the base of the nasal ala on the cleft side. There was no statistically significant difference between cleft and noncleft alar base positions on the operated side in patients who underwent the described muscular repair. Conclusions A tendon structure has been documented and demonstrated in operated patients with unilateral cleft lip and palate nose deformity; it has not been previously described in the literature. The observed outcomes after primary cleft lip repair using this structure support its utility and underscore the importance of the myrtiform muscles during unilateral cleft lip repair.

title: De-escalation of Axillary Surgery in Early Breast Cancer: Translating SOUND and INSEMA into Clinical Practice.
abstract: Objective To prospectively evaluate how often axillary staging can successfully be omitted in postmenopausal HR+/HER2- patients. Background Three randomized trials showed no difference in recurrence or survival outcomes with omission of sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) in cT1-T2N0 patients with a negative axillary ultrasound (AUS) undergoing breast-conserving surgery (BCS). We prospectively evaluated applicability of this approach. Methods From 3/1/24 to 9/1/25, SLNB was omitted in postmenopausal women age 50-70 years with unicentric or multifocal, clinical stage 1, grade 1/2, HR+/HER2- cancers and a normal AUS undergoing BCS. After the results of INSEMA were reported, tumors up to 2.5 cm were included. Patients with pathology showing grade 3, T≥3 cm, or HR- or HER2+ underwent multidisciplinary discussion regarding the need for SLNB. Results In 437 patients with 442 cancers, the median patient age was 63 years, median mammographic tumor size was 0.9 cm, and 74% were grade 2. A total of 34 patients (8%) had high-risk features on final pathology (grade 3, n=20; T≥3 cm, n=11; HER2+, n=3) and 14 (3.2%) had SLNB. Of these, 2 had SLN metastases. Objective

To prospectively evaluate how often axillary staging can successfully be omitted in postmenopausal HR+/HER2- patients.

Background

Three randomized trials showed no difference in recurrence or survival outcomes with omission of sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) in cT1-T2N0 patients with a negative axillary ultrasound (AUS) undergoing breast-conserving surgery (BCS). We prospectively evaluated applicability of this approach.
