title: A Visual LGE Extent Cutoff for Mortality Risk Stratification in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Background Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent has been linked to adverse outcomes in ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM). While quantitative methods of LGE assessment are widely accepted, semi-quantitative methods remain debated but still hold value. This study aimed to determine an optimal LGE segments cutoff for ICM patients with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <50% in a large bicentric cohort. Methods This bicentric retrospective French study included 3,591 patients with ICM (defined by prior myocardial infarction and/or coronary revascularization), LVEF <50%, and ischemic-LGE on cardiovascular magnetic resonance performed between 2008 and 2022. Ischemic LGE extent was assessed semi-quantitatively using the 17-segment model. An optimal cutoff for LGE extent was derived in the derivation cohort (Center 1, N=2,900) using a conditional inference tree and externally validated in an independent cohort (Center 2, N=691). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Prognostic performance was compared between a conventional model based on LVEF ≤35% alone and a combined model integrating LVEF ≤35% with the newly identified ischemic-LGE cutoff. Model discrimination and reclassification were assessed using Harrell's C-index, continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Results During a median follow-up of 9 years, 549 patients (15.3%) died. The optimal cutoff of visual LGE extent to predict mortality was 5 segments. Patients with high ischemic LGE extent (>5 segments) had a markedly increased risk of all-cause mortality compared with those with ≤5 segments (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.8; 95% CI: 3.0-4.8; p<0.001). Survival discrimination according to this cutoff was consistent across derivation and validation cohorts. Compared with the conventional LVEF ≤35% model alone, the combined model integrating the >5 ischemic-LGE segment cutoff significantly improved risk discrimination and patient reclassification (ΔC-index: +16%; continuous NRI: +36%; IDI: +4%; all p<0.001). Conclusion In patients with ICM, reduced LVEF (<50%), and detectable ischemic LGE, a visually assessed segment-based cutoff of >5 ischemic-LGE segments was independently associated with all-cause mortality and validated in an independent second-center cohort. This pragmatic, software-independent assessment may complement conventional risk stratification, although prospective studies are required before integration into clinical decision-making.

title: Streamline pathology foundation model by cross-magnification distillation.
abstract: Foundation models (FM) have transformed computational pathology but remain computationally prohibitive for clinical deployment due to their massive parameter counts and high-magnification processing requirements. Here, we introduce XMAG, a lightweight FM developed through cross-magnification distillation that transfers knowledge from a state-of-the-art 20x magnification teacher to an efficient 5x magnification student architecture. XMAG employs a compact backbone and operates entirely at 5x, requiring 11.3 times fewer patches per whole slide image (WSI) compared to existing approaches. Our novel distillation framework incorporates dual-level knowledge transfer, aligning both global image representations and local spatial features across magnification levels through carefully designed projection heads and spatial token mapping. We trained XMAG on 3.49 million images curated from publicly available datasets and evaluated performance across seven clinically relevant histopathology analysis tasks spanning multiple cancer types. Across four WSI-level classification tasks, XMAG achieved an average AUC within 1% of substantially larger foundation models while delivering up to 29.5-fold faster encoder-level processing, corresponding to an encoder throughput of 8.8 WSIs per minute in a controlled patch-encoding benchmark. We also found that performance differences remained task-dependent, with larger gaps observed for fine-grained tasks such as ISUP grading and patch-level phenotyping. We further explore end-to-end XMAG training as a direction for task-specific adaptation of the compact model. These results suggest that cross-magnification distillation is a promising strategy for developing efficient low-magnification pathology foundation models and may support more scalable WSI analysis in computationally constrained research and translational settings.

title: Applied nutritional investigation determinants of lower quadriceps skeletal muscle measured by ultrasound at ICU admission: a cross-sectional analysis.
abstract: Background Low skeletal muscle (SM) is common at ICU admission and is associated with worse prognosis. Early identification of at-risk patients is essential, but determinants of low SM in critically ill patients remains unclear. Objective To identify sociodemographic, nutritional, and clinical characteristics associated with low SM at ICU admission. Methods This cross-sectional analysis included critically ill patients ≥18 years admitted within 24 hours. Sociodemographic and nutritional data were obtained through anamnesis, while clinical data were extracted from records. Quadriceps muscle layer thickness (QMLT) was measured using a B-mode US. Lower QMLT was defined as values below the sex-specific 25th percentile of the sample. Binary logistic regression was performed. Results 399 patients were included (age 61.4 ± 14.9 years; 56.6% male). Older age (OR = 1.02; CI 95% 1.0-1.04), previous unintentional weight loss (OR = 1.64; CI 95% 1.03-2.61), reduced food intake before admission (OR = 2.32; CI 95% 1.44-3.74), and pressure injuries (OR = 1.83; CI 95% 1.05-3.20) were associated with low QMLT. However, in multivariate analysis, only older age (OR = 1.02; CI 95% 1.00-1.04) and reduced food intake (OR = 2.26; CI 95% 1.22-4.18) remained independent determinants. Conclusion Older age and reduced food intake were independently associated with lower QMLT at ICU admission. These findings highlight the need for early screening and targeted strategies to mitigate muscle loss and improve outcomes in critically ill patients.

title: Macular retinal layer thickness in patients with severe congenital ptosis with and without amblyopia.
abstract: Objective To evaluate macular retinal layer thickness in patients with severe congenital ptosis with and without amblyopia and compare the findings with those of healthy controls. Methods This cross-sectional study included 69 patients (87 eyes) with severe congenital ptosis, comprising 32 patients (40 eyes) with amblyopia and 37 patients (47 eyes) without amblyopia, together with 38 healthy controls (38 eyes). Macular retinal thickness was measured using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA). Automated segmentation quantified the inner five retinal layers (IRT), outer five retinal layers (ORT), and full retinal thickness (FRT) in the fovea, parafovea, and perifovea. Group differences were analyzed using analysis of covariance with adjustment for axial length (AL). Spearman rank correlation analysis was performed to assess the associations of foveal retinal thickness with AL, age, sex, and the relationship between foveal IRT and ORT. Results Compared with healthy controls, patients with amblyopia showed significantly thinner IRT in most macular regions and significantly thicker ORT across the fovea, parafovea, and perifovea (all P < 0.05). Compared with patients without amblyopia, the amblyopia group exhibited thinner IRT and thicker ORT in multiple parafoveal and perifoveal regions (all P < 0.05). Patients without amblyopia also had thicker ORT than healthy controls in the parafovea and temporal perifovea (all P < 0.05). These differences remained significant after adjustment for AL. Foveal ORT was positively correlated with foveal IRT in the amblyopia (rₛ=0.672), non-amblyopia (rₛ=0.417), and healthy control groups (rₛ=0.611) (all P ≤ 0.005). Conclusions Patients with severe congenital ptosis and amblyopia exhibit distinct alterations in macular retinal layer thickness compared with both patients without amblyopia and healthy controls. These differences persist after adjustment for axial length, suggesting that amblyopia secondary to severe congenital ptosis may lead to altered macular retinal architecture.

Foveal ORT was positively correlated with foveal IRT in the amblyopia (rₛ=0.672), non-amblyopia (rₛ=0.417), and healthy control groups (rₛ=0.611) (all P ≤ 0.005).

Conclusions

Patients with severe congenital ptosis and amblyopia exhibit distinct alterations in macular retinal layer thickness compared with both patients without amblyopia and healthy controls. These differences persist after adjustment for axial length, suggesting that amblyopia secondary to severe congenital ptosis may lead to altered macular retinal architecture.

title: Re-irradiation for recurrent high-grade glioma: current evidence and practical considerations.
abstract: Re-irradiation is an increasingly important salvage option for patients with recurrent high-grade glioma and glioblastoma, but its use is complicated by limited prospective evidence, heterogeneous treatment approaches, and concern for cumulative toxicity to the brain and critical neurologic structures. Available studies suggest that carefully selected patients may achieve meaningful local control, symptom relief, and preservation of neurologic function, although a consistent overall survival benefit has not been demonstrated. Treatment decisions therefore require individualized assessment of performance status, neurologic function, disease volume and pattern, interval from prior radiation therapy, expected prognosis, alternative salvage options, and overlap with previously irradiated organs at risk. In this expert opinion, we summarize the contemporary evidence supporting brain re-irradiation and discuss available techniques; we also describe a practical, organ-at-risk-driven framework for patient selection, target delineation, fractionation, cumulative dose assessment, and integration of systemic therapy. Re-irradiation can be delivered safely in selected patients, but treatment intensity should remain closely aligned with anatomy, prognosis, therapeutic alternatives, and patient goals.

title: Nasopharyngeal diffuse large b-cell lymphoma in a teenage presenting with cavernous sinus syndrome: A case report.
abstract: Primary lymphoma of the nasopharynx is uncommon and is more commonly seen as an association with other primary pathologies. Nasopharyngeal lymphoma is an aggressive tumor and can affect all age groups but is more commonly seen in middle-aged and older individuals. Majority of these tumors belong to the non-Hodgkin's group. Cavernous sinus syndrome (CSS) is a rare but severe complication indicating advanced aggressive stage of disease with direct extension of tumor into the cavernous sinus. Our patient is a young teenage 18-years old presented to emergency department with the symptoms of left jaw pain (4 months), facial swelling (1 month), bilateral nasal obstruction, dysphagia (1 month), visual loss in left eye and proptosis (1 week) along with weight loss. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) face and neck with contrast performed immediately revealed a nasopharyngeal mass with extension of disease into the left cavernous sinus encasing cavernous part of the left internal carotid artery (ICA), involvement of the left orbital apex, optic chiasm and pituitary gland. Histopathology later confirmed diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Laboratory investigations were unremarkable except for an elevated ESR. The patient underwent multidisciplinary management with combined chemotherapy and radiotherapy, demonstrating an excellent response on follow-up MRI and PET-CT, and was discharged with appropriate follow-up instructions. This case highlights early recognition with MRI and histopathological confirmation enables timely chemotherapy, improving outcomes and reducing the risk of permanent neurological sequelae.

title: Uncertainty-aware auto-segmentation enables adaptive radiotherapy planning of liver metastases.
abstract: Purpose Despite remarkable auto-segmentation performance and growing clinical adoption, models frequently fail to generalize beyond the training distribution. Therefore, this study aimed to develop and validate an uncertainty-aware segmentation pipeline that yields high delineation accuracy for liver cancer patients and reliably identifies safety-critical segmentation imperfections in radiotherapy. Materials and methods Datasets of n = 173 patients with 224 liver metastases were divided into training (n = 100), validation (n = 33), and test (n = 40). Each case included annotated T2-weighted magnetic resonance images. An nnU-Net segmented treatment-relevant organs and provided a margin-extended hepatic mask, which served as input to a second-stage SE-ResUNet for lesion delineation. Uncertainty was approximated via checkpoint ensembling under a cyclic learning-rate schedule, yielding entropy-based uncertainty maps and case-wise uncertainty scores. These guided an adaptive post-inference analysis consisting of (i) detection of potentially missed lesions and (ii) identification of problematic contours. Performance was evaluated on 40 patients (n = 52 lesions) using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), 95%-Hausdorff-Distance (HD95), expected calibration error (ECE), uncertainty coverage, and the correlation between case-wise uncertainty scores and segmentation accuracy. Results Overall performance across treatment-relevant organs was DSC/HD95 = 0.89/4.8 mm; lesionsegmentation achieved DSC/HD95 = 0.86/4.9 mm. Uncertainty-guided post-processing, triggered in 14/40 cases, recovered 7 initially missed metastases, increasing lesion-level sensitivity from 84.6% (44/52) to 98.1% (51/52). Uncertainty estimates showed good calibration with ECE/uncertainty coverage for organs/lesion of 7.2/93.7% and 7.5/98.3%, and significant correlation between uncertainty/DSC (r = -0.802). Conclusion The proposed pipeline seamlessly integrates accurate organ/lesion segmentation, interpretable uncertainty, and anatomy-guided post-processing to detect safety-critical segmentation failures and enable trustworthy AI auto-segmentation in clinical routine.

title: Classification of Vertebral Artery Course Variations in the Atlantoaxial Region and Their Anatomic Considerations for Surgical Planning: A CTA Imaging Analysis of 511 Patients.
abstract: Background Vertebral artery (VA) course variations in the atlantoaxial region pose significant risks during posterior C1-C2 fixation. This study aimed to classify these variations on CT angiography (CTA) and assess their anatomic implications for surgical planning. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 511 patients (1,022 vertebral arteries) who underwent cervical CTA at Beijing Tongren Hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Vertebral artery course variations were classified by two independent senior radiologists. Interobserver agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa coefficient. Associations between variation types and gender/side were analyzed using chi-square tests with adjusted standardized residuals. potential surgical implications were assessed based on anatomical relationships and literature review Results: Seven types were identified: normal type (712 arteries, 70%), high-riding type (243, 24%), posterior arch bridge type (26, 2.5%), protruding type (14, 1.4%), segmental artery type (13, 1.2%), fenestration type (9, 0.9%), and combined type (5, 0.5%). Interobserver agreement was substantial (κ = 0.795). Each type carries distinct anatomic considerations for screw placement, exposure, and surgical approach selection. Conclusions Different vertebral artery course variation types carry distinct and predictable potential surgical implications. Detailed preoperative CTA assessment with three-dimensional reconstruction is essential for identifying these variations and minimizing the risk of iatrogenic vertebral artery injury during posterior atlantoaxial surgery.

title: Ultrasound renal denervation for treatment-resistant hypertension with severe left ventricular hypertrophy.
abstract: Resistant hypertension with left ventricular hypertrophy requires aggressive treatment to reduce cardiovascular risk. Ultrasound renal denervation safely attenuates sympathetic activity and lowers blood pressure. We performed step-by-step image-guided renal denervation, demonstrating procedural feasibility, safety, and early blood pressure reduction with potential benefits for left ventricular remodeling.

title: Preparation and evaluation of degradable imaging drug loaded embolization microspheres for hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) necessitates the use of embolic agents with intrinsic radiopacity and controlled biodegradability to enhance therapeutic precision. In addressing the limitations inherent in current drug-eluting microspheres (DEMs), this study introduces the development of inherently radiopaque and biodegradable (DOX+Lipiodol) @PLGA @CaCO 3 @Alg core-shell microspheres. These microspheres were synthesized using rotating membrane emulsification and surface-induced ion crosslinking, with calcium carbonate serving multiple roles: a solid surfactant for Pickering stabilization, an acid-neutralizing agent, and an alginate shell inducer. The microspheres successfully encapsulated iodine loads, demonstrated by CT values reaching up to 8,000 HU, and contained doxorubicin at 1.53 ± 0.12 wt.%. They exhibited prolonged radiopacity for over 14 days in vivo and showed a pH-responsive drug release pattern, releasing 90% of their payload at pH 5.2 compared to 30% at pH 7.2 over 120 h. The sequential degradation process (alginate → CaCO 3 → PLGA) resulted in greater than 60% mass loss within four months, correlating with a reduction in CT attenuation. In rabbit embolization models, the microspheres achieved effective vascular occlusion and induced ischemic necrosis in ears and kidneys. CT tracking was possible without additional contrast agents, and systemic biosafety was confirmed with cell viability exceeding 90%, hemolysis below 1%, and normal hematological and histological profiles. These findings suggest that the microspheres could serve as a clinically translatable platform for image-guided TACE, integrating occlusion, therapy, and monitoring into a cohesive treatment strategy.

title: Robot-assisted total laparoscopic pancreaticoduodenectomy with transvaginal specimen extraction: a case report.
abstract: Natural orifice specimen extraction surgery reduces incision-related complications and accelerates postoperative recovery while maintaining oncologic safety, whereas the da Vinci robotic surgical system further enhances the precision of minimally invasive procedures. This case report describes a robot-assisted total laparoscopic pancreaticoduodenectomy combined with transvaginal specimen extraction (RPD-TVSE). The patient was a 64-year-old female with moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the descending duodenum. The procedure took 350 min, with intraoperative blood loss of 200 mL; no blood transfusion was administered during the perioperative period. The patient was able to ambulate on postoperative day 1, with no adverse events recorded. Histopathology confirmed tumor staging as pT2N0M0, with all surgical margins negative. At 12-month follow-up, no evidence of recurrence was observed. This case demonstrates that RPD-TVSE is technically feasible and yields favorable short-term outcomes, providing a novel minimally invasive surgical option for female patients. However, long-term oncologic safety requires further investigation and validation.

title: Comparative accuracy of imaging modalities for differentiating malignant small testicular masses.
abstract: Objectives To synthesise evidence comparing the diagnostic performance of imaging modalities in differentiating malignant from benign small testicular masses. Patients and methods A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant search of PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane and Web of Science databases up to 6 May 2026 identified 11 studies comprising 707 patients with small testicular masses (predominantly <2 cm) who underwent imaging prior to a histopathological or, where unavailable, a mixed clinical/radiological follow-up reference standard. Diagnostic accuracy measures for six modalities (brightness-mode [B-Mode] ultrasonography [US], colour doppler US [CDUS], contrast-enhanced US [CEUS], magnetic resonance imaging [MRI], strain elastography [SE] and strain ratio [SR]) were synthesised using a Bayesian bivariate hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic model. Results The CEUS demonstrated the most reliable discriminatory ability with a pooled sensitivity of 91% and pooled specificity of 81%, yielding the highest diagnostic odds ratio of 46. B-Mode US remains a valid screening test with the highest sensitivity of 96% but a specificity of only 39%. CDUS showed a pooled sensitivity of 69% and a specificity of 81%. MRI had a pooled sensitivity of 91% and a specificity of 38%. SE demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 87% and a specificity of 56%. Finally, SR reported the lowest sensitivity at 74% and a specificity of 50%. CEUS demonstrated significantly higher specificity than B-Mode US (ratio 1.9, 95% posterior interval [PI] 1.2-4.4) and MRI (ratio 1.8, 95% PI 1.0-5.2). Conclusion The CEUS demonstrates the highest combined sensitivity and specificity for differentiating benign from malignant testicular masses, significantly outperforming conventional B-Mode US and MRI in specificity. Objectives

To synthesise evidence comparing the diagnostic performance of imaging modalities in differentiating malignant from benign small testicular masses.

Patients and methods

A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant search of PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane and Web of Science databases up to 6 May 2026 identified 11 studies comprising 707 patients with small testicular masses (predominantly <2 cm) who underwent imaging prior to a histopathological or, where unavailable, a mixed clinical/radiological follow-up reference standard. Diagnostic accuracy measures for six modalities (brightness-mode [B-Mode] ultrasonography [US], colour doppler US [CDUS], contrast-enhanced US [CEUS], magnetic resonance imaging [MRI], strain elastography [SE] and strain ratio [SR]) were synthesised using a Bayesian bivariate hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic model.

Results

The CEUS demonstrated the most reliable discriminatory ability with a pooled sensitivity of 91% and pooled specificity of 81%, yielding the highest diagnostic odds ratio of 46. B-Mode US remains a valid screening test with the highest sensitivity of 96% but a specificity of only 39%. CDUS showed a pooled sensitivity of 69% and a specificity of 81%. MRI had a pooled sensitivity of 91% and a specificity of 38%. SE demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 87% and a specificity of 56%. Finally, SR reported the lowest sensitivity at 74% and a specificity of 50%. CEUS demonstrated significantly higher specificity than B-Mode US (ratio 1.9, 95% posterior interval [PI] 1.2-4.4) and MRI (ratio 1.8, 95% PI 1.0-5.2).

The CEUS demonstrates the highest combined sensitivity and specificity for differentiating benign from malignant testicular masses, significantly outperforming conventional B-Mode US and MRI in specificity. title: The Solitary Functioning Kidney: From Pathophysiology to Long-Term Management.
abstract: Solitary functioning kidney (SFK) is a clinical condition characterized by the presence of a single functioning kidney, arising from either congenital anomalies or acquired causes. It is recognized as an important risk factor for chronic kidney disease (CKD) and, in some patients, for progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). Congenital solitary functioning kidney is commonly associated with renal hypoplasia or dysplasia, genetic abnormalities, and congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract, whereas acquired solitary functioning kidney is often secondary to unilateral nephrectomy for renal tumors, trauma, tuberculosis, severe infection, or living kidney donation. The principal pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the progression from SFK to CKD are compensatory renal hypertrophy and glomerular hyperfiltration in the remnant kidney. Although these adaptive responses may initially maintain renal function, sustained compensation can lead to glomerular injury, proteinuria, tubulointerstitial damage, and renal fibrosis. Early diagnosis relies primarily on imaging modalities, such as ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging, together with assessment of renal function and emerging biomarkers, including neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and cystatin C. Prognostic evaluation of patients with SFK should comprehensively consider etiology, age, compensatory renal growth, associated urinary tract anomalies, comorbidities, and markers of kidney injury. Effective long-term management is essential to prevent or delay progression to CKD and ESKD, with particular emphasis on individualized follow-up, lifestyle modification, blood pressure control, reduction of proteinuria, and avoidance of additional nephrotoxic insults. Previous publications have often addressed pediatric congenital solitary functioning kidney (CSFK), living kidney donors, and disease-related nephrectomy cohorts separately, limiting the translation of heterogeneous evidence into a common clinical approach. This review integrates congenital and acquired SFK across the life course, distinguishes shared markers of established kidney injury from etiology-specific determinants of renal reserve, and proposes an evidence-informed framework for dynamic risk stratification and risk-adapted follow-up and management. This framework is conceptual and requires prospective validation.

title: Surface-extraction MRI of the fetal brain: an improved approach for diagnosing anomalies associated with antenatal absence of the septum pellucidum.
abstract: Introduction Prenatal imaging is crucial for evaluating neurological development in cases of absence of septum pellucidum (ASP), which may be associated with a spectrum of cortical, cerebellar and ocular anomalies and variable neurodevelopmental outcomes. Recent advances in fetal MRI techniques have improved the detection and characterization of subtle brain abnormalities. Case report A pregnant patient was referred to our tertiary centre for targeted neurosonography at 28weeks of gestation, confirming ASP initially considered isolated. Fetal MRI at 33 weeks suspected associated cortical malformations, with unilateral peri-sylvian polymicrogyria and closed lip schizencephaly, but it partially limited by motion artefacts. Subsequent super‑resolution reconstruction (SRR) and cortical surface extraction confirmed the presence of polymicrogyria associated with schizencephaly. Post-MRI neurosonography also confirmed unilateral perisylvian polymicrogyria and schizencephaly. Following multidisciplinary discussion parents opted for termination of pregnancy. Post‑mortem neuropathological examination confirmed the imaging findings, demonstrating polymicrogyria associated with schizencephaly in the right perisylvian region. Conclusion This case highlights the possible added diagnostic value of advanced fetal MRI post‑processing, which enabled precise characterization of cortical abnormalities not confidently identified on conventional imaging. The strong correlation with neuropathological findings supports the potential role of surface‑based analysis in improving diagnostic accuracy and prenatal counselling in cases of ASP.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract: Background Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. Methods In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. Results Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted P <0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). Conclusions In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. Registration URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn/. Unique identifier: ChiCTR2300074640.

title: Thoracic Intermuscular Adiposity, Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction, and Prognosis After Cardiac Surgery.
abstract: Background Body mass index is a widely-used yet imprecise measure of adiposity. Thoracic intermuscular adiposity is reported to be related with coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD), but their prognostic implications after cardiac surgery are not clear. This study aimed to investigate whether computed tomography-derived thoracic intermuscular adiposity and CMD provide better prognostic information than body mass index in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. Methods This study consecutively enrolled 666 patients undergoing elective surgery from 3 centers. Using computed tomography at the T12 vertebral level, we quantified the cross-sectional areas (cm 2 ) of skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue, and intermuscular adipose tissue. Intermuscular fat fraction was calculated as intermuscular adipose tissue/(intermuscular adipose tissue+skeletal muscle)×100%. CMD was defined by a coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance >25. The primary end point was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and rehospitalization for heart failure. Results A total of 63 MACEs (9.5%) occurred during a median 17-month follow-up. Obesity defined by body mass index (10.7% of patients) was not associated with MACE ( P =0.187). Each 1% increase in intermuscular fat fraction was significantly associated with CMD (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.14-1.31]; P <0.001), whereas body mass index showed no such correlation ( P =0.964). CMD independently predicted MACE (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.03; [95% CI: 1.15-3.61]; P = 0.015), whereas intermuscular fat fraction did not ( P =0.516). The annualized MACE rate was significantly higher in patients with CMD (11.0% versus 5.2%, P =0.004). Conclusions Computed tomography-derived intermuscular adiposity correlated strongly with CMD, and preprocedural CMD was associated with a higher risk of MACE after cardiac surgery. External validation and prospective studies are warranted.

title: Delayed Multi-Compartment Traumatic Hernias After Blunt Abdominal Trauma: A Case-Based Review of Diagnosis and Staged Management.
abstract: BackgroundTraumatic diaphragmatic hernias (TDHs) and traumatic abdominal wall hernias (TAWHs) are uncommon sequelae of blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) and may be missed during the initial evaluation. Delayed presentation can occur months to years later, resulting in incarceration, obstruction, or respiratory compromise.Case PresentationA 61-year-old woman presented 1 year after a motor vehicle collision with abdominal pain, nausea, constipation, and dyspnea. Computed tomography demonstrated an incarcerated left diaphragmatic hernia containing colon and omentum, along with a right flank hernia containing ascending colon. Review of prior imaging revealed a flank hematoma and subtle abdominal wall disruption at the time of initial injury. The patient underwent urgent laparoscopic repair of the diaphragmatic hernia followed by elective robotic transabdominal preperitoneal repair of the flank hernia 2 months later.DiscussionThis case illustrates a pattern of delayed multi-compartment traumatic herniation resulting from thoracoabdominal force transmission. Diagnostic delays may occur because of competing priorities during polytrauma management, limitations of initial imaging, and delayed development of herniation, especially when the injuries are subtle. Findings such as rib fractures, pneumothorax, abdominal wall hematoma, and persistent symptoms should prompt continued surveillance.ConclusionDelayed multi-compartment traumatic hernias represent a diagnostic challenge requiring a high index of suspicion, longitudinal surveillance, and individualized management. A staged operative approach based on symptom severity and anatomic location can effectively address differing levels of clinical urgency.
